name: supersession
wording: the only change to a concept, its name included, to a context's description or to the purpose: a new version restating it whole, never edited in place or extended; a concept renamed stays one concept, its earlier names in its history; its reason is why; two versions superseding one compete until a later one supersedes both
reason: The lead found that correcting a name, as a redefined term is corrected, had no form: a concept keeps its identity when it takes its Cratylic name, so a rename is a new version of it, never a retirement and a new concept.
